tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Order passed by: Additional Commissioner, CGST & C.EX., Palghar Commissionerate, Office of the Commissioner of CGST, Palghar, 5th floor, Plot No. C-24, Sector-E, Central GST Bhavan, Bandra-Kurla Complex, Bandra (East), Mumbai-400 051. Appeal to be filed before: Commissioner CGST & CX, (Appeals) III, Mumbai having his office at 9th floor, Piramal Chambers, Lalbaug Lower Parel, Mumbai – 400 012. Background of the case and brief details of dispute / litigation: The Company in the course of its retail lending business, leveraged its vast pan India network (i.e. branches, meeting centres and Dealers/DSA network and other touch points) to provide marketing and brand promotion support services to promote various insurance products for a service fee consideration. Such activity was an integral part of the loan sourcing activity carried out by the Company’s network across India. The Company had duly paid applicable GST on such service fees consideration. In respect of such services, the Company had received a penalty demand order u/s 122(1)(ii) of Rs. 1,12,01,85,000 from Additional Commissioner, CGST & C.EX., Palghar Commissionerate, Office of the Commissioner of CGST, Palghar stating that the Company has allegedly raised invoices without actual rendering of services. Based on consultation with tax expert, the Company was of the view that the said demand was not tenable and was liable to set-aside as the Company had duly rendered such marketing and brand promotion services.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Additional Commissioner, CGST & C.EX., Palghar Commissionerate, Office of the Commissioner of CGST, Palghar, 5th floor, Plot No. C-24, Sector-E, Central GST Bhavan, Bandra-Kurla Complex, Bandra (East), Mumbai-400 051
tax_litigation.status: he Company received an order in Appeal dated January 30, 2026 from Commissioner, CGST and Central Excise, Appeal III, Mumbai wherein order passed by Additional Commissioner, CGST & C. Ex., Palghar Commissionerate, dated February 03, 2025 (received by the Company vide email dated February 4, 2025 at around 11:20 a.m. (IST) and intimated to the stock exchanges on February 05, 2025), in respect of marketing and brand promotion services provided by L&T Finance to insurance companies was upheld. It was a consolidated order and covered all parties. Based on consultation with tax expert, the Company is of the view that the said demand is not tenable. Accordingly, the Company is in process of filing an appeal against the order before the second appellate authority i.e. before the Goods and Services Tax Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT) after paying requisite pre-deposit of 10%.

operating_notes.text: Retail book was ₹1,19,508 Cr at FY26 end, up 26% YoY, with retailisation at 98% of the overall book.
NIMs + Fees was 10.47% in Q4FY26 vs 10.41% in Q3FY26; Q4FY26 credit cost was 2.64% vs 2.83% in Q3FY26.
Gold Finance exited Q4FY26 with 330 branches, 200 added since the June 2025 acquisition; PLANET app crossed 2.40 Crore downloads.
Retail book stands at ₹1,19,508 Cr at the end of FY26, a growth of 26% YoY.
Retail book reached ₹1,19,508 Cr, up 26% YoY, with total book at ₹1,21,728 Cr.
Unique customer franchise stands at about 2.8 crore at the end of FY26 after adding 8.3 lakh new customers in Q4FY26.

Project Cyclops has underwritten over ₹12,000 Cr in Two Wheeler Finance over two years and is live in Farm Equipment, Personal Loans and SME; rollout to Rural Business Finance and Mortgage is planned for FY27.
Gold Finance network expanded to 343 branches, with ~500 new branches planned in FY27; book reached ₹3,829 Cr, up 182% YoY.
CGFMU and CGTMSE coverage commenced for select Rural Business Finance and SME cohorts; CGFMU to cover 35–40% of FY27 microfinance disbursements.
Co-lending arrangements: 1,65,804 outstanding cases, gross outstanding ₹2,188.10 Cr, weighted average rate 11.99%, sector Personal Loan, non-performing ₹31.41 Cr as at Sep-2026.
PLANET app surpassed 2.7 crore downloads, services 94% of customer service requests and drove collections of ₹2,168 Cr in Q2FY27.
Gold Finance exited Q2FY27 with 502 branches, a cumulative addition of 372 since the June 2025 acquisition.
Project Helios cut underwriting turnaround from 21 to 16 hours for SEP and 37 to 22 hours for SENP, processing about 80,000 files.
Allotted ₹1,500 Cr of senior secured NCDs at 7.8384% coupon maturing September 2029.

timeline.summary: L&T Finance allotted ₹500 Cr of senior secured rated listed redeemable NCDs on April 21, 2026.
L&T Finance Limited’s Board recommended a final dividend of ₹2.75 per equity share (₹10 face value) for FY2025-26, pending AGM approval.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹4,771.03 Cr, net profit ₹809.16 Cr (+27.3% YoY).
L&T Finance reported Q4FY26 consolidated PAT of ₹807 Cr with retail book growth of 26% YoY to ₹1,19,508 Cr.
On April 29, 2026, L&T Finance announced the exercise of a call option to redeem ₹15 Cr of subordinated perpetual NCDs on June 3, 2026.
L&T Finance reported Q4FY26 consolidated PAT of ₹807 Cr and highest-ever annual PAT of ₹3,003 Cr, alongside unveiling its Lakshya 2031 strategic plan.
L&T Finance Limited’s 18th AGM on May 29, 2026, adopted financial statements and declared ₹2.16/share final dividend with 99.99% approval.
L&T Finance reported Q1FY27 consolidated PAT of ₹902 Cr, up 29% YoY, on a 27% larger book of ₹1,29,634 Cr, and reiterated its 2.8% RoA target for Q4FY27.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹5,484.23 Cr (+26.5% YoY), net profit ₹972.76 Cr (+32.4% YoY).
L&T Finance reported Q2FY27 consolidated PAT of ₹975 Cr, up 33% YoY, on a 28% larger book of ₹1,36,635 Cr, with GS3 at 2.75% and WACB down to 6.95%.
L&T Finance reported Q2FY27 consolidated net profit of ₹975 Cr, up 33% YoY, driven by a 28% expansion in the loan book.
